wu: Tech Charades: Students draw a tech word (phone, laptop, game) from a hat and act it out without speaking. Others guess 'Is it a phone?' or 'Is it a game?'
wuAlt: Tech Pictionary: Students draw a tech device on the board for others to name
Tech Word Race: Two teams race to write 5 tech words on the board
pres: Show flashcards of tech devices (phone, laptop, tablet, TV). Model sentences: 'I like using my phone.' 'I love playing games.' 'I hate watching TV.' Students repeat chorally. Check understanding with thumbs up/down: 'Do you like using a laptop?'
presAlt: Realia Demo: Show a phone and say 'I like taking photos' then ask students to say what they like doing with it
Story: Draw a simple comic of a teen using devices and model sentences from the speech bubbles
prac: Match-Up Game: Students match device cards to verb phrases (using, watching, playing). Then in pairs, they ask 'Do you like using a phone?' and respond with 'Yes, I do' or 'No, I don't'
pracAlt: Sentence Relay: Teams race to write correct sentences like 'I love watching TV' on the board
Tech Survey Prep: Students fill in a simple grid with 'like/love/hate' for 3 devices
ls: Listen to a short audio of two teens talking about their tech habits. Students tick boxes on a worksheet for 'likes' and 'dislikes' (e.g., 'Ahmed likes playing games').
re: Device Freeze: Teacher calls out a device (e.g., 'laptop'), students mime using it. When teacher says 'freeze!', they stop. Last one moving sits down.
prod: Tech Survey Creation: In groups, students design a 3-question survey about tech habits (e.g., 'Do you like using a phone?'). They ask 3 classmates and report back to the class: 'Fatima likes using a phone'
rw: Read a simple bar graph showing 'tech habits' (e.g., 5 students like phones, 2 hate tablets). Students write 2 sentences: '5 students like phones.' '2 students hate tablets.'
st: Sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' but replace body parts with tech words: 'Phone, laptop, tablet, mouse!' End with 'Good job today! You can talk about tech habits. Thank you, class!'
g: Act out a tech device without speaking for others to guess
Match device cards to verb phrases like 'using' or 'playing'
Mime using a device when called, freeze on command
Groups race to ask classmates 3 tech habit questions
Teams race to write correct 'like/love/hate' sentences
diff: Fast finishers: Write 2 more sentences about their family's tech habits
Support learners: Use sentence frames 'I like ___. I love ___. I hate ___.' with word bank
hw: Draw 3 tech devices and write 'I like/love/hate ___' for each
Ask 5 family members 'Do you like using ___?' and write their answers
Write 4 sentences about your daily tech habits (e.g., 'I use my phone every day')
tip: Use local tech examples like mobile apps popular in Morocco (e.g., TikTok, WhatsApp) to make the theme relevant and increase engagement.
